claude.sample_unit: runs (28 synthetic vignettes x 4 personas x 2 repeats)

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM clinical reasoning and safety to persona prompt framing variations
links.effect: Contraindication/sequencing violations occurred only in high time-pressure/lean-efficiency framing: 8/56 runs (14.3%), and 8/8 trap-case runs versus 0/24 in the other three conditions.
links.quote: Restricting the analysis to the 32 trap-case runs, violations occurred in eight of the eight high/lean runs and in none of the 24 trap-case runs under the other three conditions.

links.outcome: Unsafe action-sequencing/contraindication violations (e.g., antithrombotic before excluding aortic dissection) in trap cases
links.effect: Violations in 8/56 high/lean runs (14.3%), none elsewhere; mean severity among trap-case violations was 2.75 on the 3-point scale.
links.quote: The mean severity among trap-case violations was 2.75 on the three-point scale.

links.outcome: Differential diagnosis completeness and top-ranked accuracy across prompt conditions
links.effect: Gold diagnosis was in the top five in all runs; top-ranked accuracy lowest in high/lean (50/56, 89.3%) versus 100% in safety-first conditions; high time pressure narrowed differential entropy (beta -0.246).
links.quote: Top-ranked accuracy was high overall but was lowest in the high/lean condition (50 of 56 runs, 89.3%) (Table 3 ).

links.effect: Trap-case violations were 8/8 under high/lean versus 0/24 under other prompt conditions.
links.quote: Restricting the analysis to the 32 trap-case runs, violations occurred in eight of the eight high/lean runs and in none of the 24 trap-case runs under the other three conditions.

links.effect: Violations occurred only in high/lean: 8 of 56 runs (14.3%).
links.quote: Contraindication or sequencing violations were observed only in the high/lean condition, where they occurred in eight of 56 runs (14.3%).

links.effect: Among discharges, safety-first scored 4.5 versus lean 2.6 on a five-point scale.
links.quote: When discharge was recommended, safety-first prompting produced more specific safety-net instructions than lean prompting (mean score 4.5 versus 2.6 on a five-point scale; Figure 4 ).
